sections.title: What is Agent Store
sections.body: Agent Store is an "app store + local management client" for Claude Code / Codex. The web store in the browser is for discovering and searching; the desktop client on your machine manages installed resources, shows usage and runs the built-in local relay. You can install three kinds of resources:
bullets: Skills: workflows and expertise added to Claude Code / Codex
MCP servers: external tools and data sources connected through the Model Context Protocol
Providers: model access configurations, including your own API key and upstream address

sections.title: Install the desktop client
sections.body: Get the macOS (Universal, works on Apple silicon and Intel), Windows or Linux (.deb / .rpm) desktop client from the download page. The client manages installed resources on this machine, maintains provider configurations, runs the local relay and shows usage.
bullets: The installers are currently unsigned, so the system blocks them on first launch. This is expected; the files are not damaged
If macOS says the app "is damaged and can't be opened": drag the app into "Applications", run xattr -cr "/Applications/Agent Store.app" in Terminal, then double-click to open it
If Windows shows "Unknown publisher": click "More info", then "Run anyway"
These prompts will go away once Apple / Windows code signing is in place

sections.title: Browse and install in the store
sections.body: The store page is a table with one package per row, showing category, publisher and installs. At the top you can switch category, show only packages from verified publishers, and sort by installs / date added; press / to search.
bullets: Click a row to open details on the right: what runs after installation, install command, specs and README
"Install" first tries to open the desktop client; if no client is detected, it copies the install command and prompts you to download

sections.title: Where the three resource types are installed
sections.body: Installing downloads the resource to the ~/.agent-store directory on your machine (with subdirectories for skills, MCP and providers), then connects it to the tools you choose by type: skills are linked into each tool's skills directory, MCP servers and providers are written into each tool's config. When enabling a resource, you specify which tool it applies to (Claude Code or Codex).
bullets: Skills: the whole skill directory is kept once in ~/.agent-store/skills/<slug>/, and each tool you enable gets a symlink to it: ~/.claude/skills/<name> for Claude Code, ~/.codex/skills/<name> for Codex
MCP: the server entry is written into the tool config: mcpServers in ~/.claude.json for Claude Code, mcp_servers in ~/.codex/config.toml for Codex
Providers: registered as an editable access configuration (API key, upstream address, model mapping, etc.), which takes effect through the local relay once enabled

sections.title: Local relay
sections.body: The local relay (local) is central to using providers. Once enabled, it points the API address of Claude Code / Codex to a loopback port on this machine (default http://127.0.0.1:18780, listening only on 127.0.0.1). Requests go to the local relay first and are then forwarded to the real upstream according to the provider configuration.
bullets: No need to give the CLI your real API key: the relay gives the CLI a placeholder token, and the real credential stays only in the local provider configuration, attached by the relay when forwarding
Model mapping and allowlist: rewrite the model name in the request to one the upstream supports, or have a provider handle only models in its allowlist
Usage metering: input / output / cache tokens, cost, latency and status code are recorded for each request
You can have multiple listener configurations, each on its own port (starting at 18780 by default, adding 100 for each)

sections.title: Level priority and fallback
sections.body: Each provider configuration has a Level (an integer; lower means higher priority; default 1). A request first selects candidate providers from the lowest Level up and tries the highest-priority one first; when a candidate fails, it moves to the next. It switches to the next candidate when:
bullets: A network-level error occurs, such as connection refused or DNS failure
The upstream returns a 5xx
The requested model is not in this provider's allowlist

sections.title: Command line
sections.body: You can install and manage resources without opening the desktop client: install a resource with install, apply it to a tool with enable, then write enabled resources into the tool config with sync.
sections.code:
aas install <id|slug>           # Install from the catalog
aas list                        # List installed
aas search <query>              # Search the catalog
aas info <slug>                 # Show resource details
aas enable <slug> --for claude  # Enable for Claude Code
aas disable <slug> --for codex  # Disable for Codex
aas sync                        # Write enabled resources into tool config
aas relay start|stop|status     # Manage the local relay
aas usage --days 7              # Show usage and cost
aas update [slug]               # Update installed resources

sections.title: Usage dashboard
sections.body: The overview page of the desktop client summarizes the usage recorded by the local relay: consumption trend (today / last 7 days / last 30 days), total cost, total tokens, total requests and model distribution, plus the local relay's listening address, today's requests, success rate and on/off switch. Recent requests are listed one by one with app, model → provider, latency and status code. On the command line, aas usage shows the same summary and can filter by days, provider or tool.

sections.title: Pro features
sections.body: A Pro subscription unlocks usage governance:
bullets: Budgets and overspend alerts: set a budget cap per provider and get alerted when nearing or exceeding it
Usage analytics and export: more detailed cost / token analysis and data export
Smart routing: failover across any number of providers, skipping the ones that failed recently
Multi-key rotation: configure several API keys for one provider and take turns with them to spread single-key rate limits

sections.title: Subscriptions and lifetime purchase
sections.body: Browsing, installing, the local relay and the usage dashboard are free for everyone. If you need Pro, you can subscribe monthly or yearly, or make a one-time lifetime purchase:
bullets: Free: browse and install resources, local relay forwarding (failover across up to two providers), usage dashboard
Pro monthly: {monthly} / month
Pro yearly: {yearly} / year
Lifetime: {lifetime}, pay once, Pro forever
Cancel or resume on the Subscription tab of your dashboard. After canceling, Pro stays until the period ends and can be resumed until then; orders and payments are on Waffo's billing page
